initialize_result.instructions: Evendo is a worldwide guide to restaurants, bars, shops, attractions and landmarks, organised as Country > Region > City > Neighbourhood > Venue. All results are read-only data from evendo.com. Workflow: (1) resolve_place to turn a place name into an ID; (2) find_venues with that ID and filters, or search_venues for keyword matching (e.g. 'ramen', 'rooftop'); (3) get_venue for full details, links and booking URL, or get_venues to load many at once (e.g. a whole itinerary). Never search for venues by putting a city name in the text ('restaurants in Prague'): resolve the place, then scope by its ID. Text search is keyword-based with English stemming but no typo tolerance and no semantic matching. Each venue appears once per result list, even though Evendo stores a copy of it for every list page it is featured on. Sorting: default is Evendo ranking (most prominent first); use sort_by for place_score (overall quality), rating, most reviewed, or distance. min_place_score keeps only high-quality venues. Mapping everyday words to filters: cheap/budget -> price_level inexpensive; upscale -> expensive or very_expensive; kid-friendly/family -> audience Family Friendly or Child Friendly; dog-friendly -> audience Pet Friendly; wheelchair -> audience Wheelchair Accessible; outdoor/terrace -> environment Outdoor; sunset -> style_visual Sunset Spots; views/panoramic -> style_visual Iconic Views or Panoramas; pub -> Bars + location_type Pub; cafe -> Restaurants + location_type Cafe; museum/gallery/park -> Attractions + category Museum/Gallery/Park; market -> Shopping + category Market; good ratings -> min_rating 4 + min_reviews 10; top rated -> min_rating 4.5 + min_reviews 20. Rooftop, waterfront, live music etc. have no filter: use search_venues. If one value of a field conflicts with another (e.g. 'vegan fine dining', both are categories), filter on the rarer one and check the other in the results, or use search_venues with both words. There are no counts or aggregates: to answer 'how many', page through find_venues until has_more is false; to compare two places, fetch each with the same filters and compare the results yourself.

tools.name: resolve_place
tools.title: Resolve a place name
tools.description: Find the Evendo ID of a country, region, city or neighbourhood by name. Always call this first: other tools take place IDs, not names. Names can be ambiguous (several 'Soho's), so check address_city / country_code in the results and pick the right one. If you don't know what kind of place it is, omit place_type.

place_type.description: Cities for cities, Neighbourhoods for districts, CountryRegions for regions like Scotland or Bavaria (if none found, try Regions, then omit place_type), Destinations for destination areas, Country for countries.

tools.name: find_venues
tools.title: Find venues in a place
tools.description: List venues of one type anywhere inside a place (country, region, city or neighbourhood), best-ranked first, or nearest-first when `near` is given; sort_by switches to highest rated, most reviewed or distance. Use for requests like 'top-rated cheap Italian restaurants in Prague', 'most reviewed bars in London' or 'family-friendly outdoor attractions in Scotland'. place_id must come from resolve_place. For keyword matching ('sushi', 'rooftop', 'craft beer'), use search_venues instead. If a neighbourhood returns fewer than ~5 results, widen to its city.

venue_type.description: Restaurants (incl. cafes, diners), Bars (pubs, nightclubs), Shopping (markets, shops), Attractions (museums, parks, galleries, zoos), Landmarks (monuments, historic sites). Unsure between Attractions and Landmarks? Try both.

category.description: Exact, case-sensitive category. Restaurants: "Italian", "Japanese", "Mexican", "Indian", "Chinese", "Thai", "French", "Mediterranean", "Seafood", "Steakhouse", "Pizza", "Sushi", "Vegan", "Vegetarian", "Fast Food", "Fine Dining". Bars: "Cocktail Bar", "Wine Bar", "Sports Bar", "Beer Garden". Shopping: "Market", "Boutique", "Mall". Attractions: "Museum", "Park", "Gallery", "Zoo", "Theme Park", "Garden". If unsure of the exact value, use search_venues text instead.

location_type.description: Finer type than venue_type, exact match, e.g. "Pub", "Cafe", "Restaurant", "Attraction", "Gastropub", "Museum". Pub = Bars + "Pub"; cafe / coffee shop = Restaurants + "Cafe".

price_level.description: "cheap"/"budget" = inexpensive; "upscale"/"fancy" = expensive or very_expensive. There is no "free" level; for free places use search_venues with text "free".

min_rating.description: Minimum average rating, 0-5. "good" = 4.0, "top rated"/"best" = 4.5 (pair with min_reviews).

min_reviews.description: Minimum number of reviews; use ~50+ to avoid thinly-rated places. "good" = 10+, "top rated" = 20+.

environment.description: "outdoor"/"terrace"/"al fresco" = Outdoor. For "outdoor seating" make two calls, Outdoor and "Indoor and Outdoor", and merge.

ambience.description: Atmosphere tags. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

audience.description: Who the place suits / accessibility. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

amenities.description: Required amenities. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

experience.description: Experience tags. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

sustainability.description: Sustainability tags. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

weather_suitability.description: Weather suitability. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

access.description: Physical access difficulty. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

style_visual.description: Views. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

style_social_media.description: Photo / social-media appeal. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

style_architecture.description: Architecture. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

style_aesthetic.description: Interior / design aesthetic. Every listed value must be present (AND), so pass only what the user actually requires.

min_place_score.description: Minimum Evendo place score (0-100 overall quality; most venues are 20-50, 70+ is excellent, 90+ is a city's very best).

near.description: Restrict to this radius around a point; results then sort nearest-first unless sort_by says otherwise. For 'near <landmark>', first find the landmark with search_venues (venue_type Landmarks, then Attractions) and use its location.

sort_by.description: best (default): Evendo ranking, or nearest-first when `near` is given. place_score: highest Evendo place score (0-100 overall quality) first. rating: highest average rating first (pair with min_reviews so 1-review places don't win). reviews: most reviewed first ('most popular'). nearest / farthest: by distance, require `near`. Places missing the value sort last. Changing sort_by restarts pagination: don't reuse a cursor from another sort.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous call with otherwise identical arguments. Never invent one.

tools.name: search_venues
tools.title: Keyword search for venues
tools.description: Keyword search over venue names, taglines and descriptions (stemmed; 'brewery' matches 'breweries'; no typo tolerance). Scope it with within_place_id (from resolve_place) — never put the city name in the text. Short, concrete keywords work best: 'ramen', 'rooftop bar', 'flea market'. Combine with filters and/or `near`.

within_place_id.description: Restrict to this place's subtree (city, neighbourhood, region, country).

venue_type.description: Restaurants (incl. cafes, diners), Bars (pubs, nightclubs), Shopping (markets, shops), Attractions (museums, parks, galleries, zoos), Landmarks (monuments, historic sites). Unsure between Attractions and Landmarks? Try both. Omit for vague asks ('spots', 'places').

tools.name: list_subareas
tools.title: List areas inside a place
tools.description: List the direct children of a place, e.g. the neighbourhoods of a city or the cities of a region, most prominent first. Useful to suggest areas to explore or to narrow a search.

area_type.description: e.g. Neighbourhoods for a city, Cities for a region, CountryRegions for a country. Omit to see everything one level down, which can include featured venues, not just areas.

tools.name: get_venue
tools.title: Get venue details
tools.description: Full details for one venue or place: description, address, coordinates, phone, website, booking link, photos, and all attribute tags. Pass the id from a previous result (or a slug like 'united-kingdom/london'). For several venues at once, use get_venues.

id.description: Node ID from another tool's results.

slug.description: Evendo slug path, if you have it instead of an ID.

tools.name: get_venues
tools.title: Get details for several venues
tools.description: Full details (same fields as get_venue) for up to 50 venues or places in one call, e.g. every stop of an itinerary. Pass ids and/or slugs from previous results; duplicates are fetched once. Results keep the order you passed (ids first, then slugs); anything not found is listed in not_found instead of failing the call.

ids.description: Node IDs from other tools' results.

slugs.description: Evendo slug paths, if you have them instead of IDs.
